status: curated investigation pathways; not full courses
principle: Accessible entry is distinct from depth of formal analysis

year4.label: Year 4

investigations.start: Highlight the 4-times table. What repeats?
investigations.investigate: Compare multiples of 2, 4 and 8. Which highlighted cells do they share?
investigations.deeper: Explain why every multiple of 8 is also a multiple of 4. Try another pair.
investigations.practical: Counters and a printed hundred square.

investigations.start: Arrange 12 counters into a rectangle. Can you make another?
investigations.investigate: Find every rectangle for 24. Decide whether turning a rectangle makes a new factor pair.
investigations.deeper: Which numbers make only one rectangle, apart from turning it?
investigations.practical: 24 counters or small paper squares.

investigations.start: Make a rectangle with a perimeter of 36 units. Count its sides.
investigations.investigate: Keep the perimeter fixed and change the rectangle. Is the area always the same?
investigations.deeper: Find the largest area using whole-number sides. Explain how you checked them all.
investigations.practical: 36 matchsticks or a loop of string on squared paper.

investigations.start: Make two different shapes using five squares.
investigations.investigate: Compare shapes with the same area. Do their perimeters match?
investigations.deeper: Explain which shared edges reduce the outside perimeter.
investigations.practical: Five paper squares per person.

investigations.curriculumConnection: Counting, grouping and spatial reasoning · enrichment
investigations.start: Paint a 2 × 2 × 2 cube. Inspect one small cube.
investigations.investigate: Try a 3 × 3 × 3 cube. Sort by the number of painted faces; count each group.
investigations.deeper: Can you predict which cubes have no paint before looking inside? No formula needed.
investigations.practical: Small cubes; colour the outside of a paper cube model.

investigations.start: Make a guess and explain what one clue tells you.
investigations.investigate: Keep a short list of what you know. Make a guess to test one idea.
investigations.deeper: Can an unsuccessful guess still be useful? Show an example.
investigations.practical: Coloured counters and a paper recording grid.

year4.gaps: Existing workshops retained; coverage and assessment require further development.

year5.label: Year 5

investigations.curriculumConnection: Multiplication and division A · factors and primes
investigations.start: Split 24 into two factors, then keep splitting.
investigations.investigate: Start with a different factor pair. Compare the prime leaves.
investigations.deeper: Explain why the order changes but the prime factors do not.
investigations.practical: Number cards and string to connect a tree.

investigations.start: Build a cuboid with 30 cubes. Record its three dimensions.
investigations.investigate: Find all the cuboids with volume 30. How will you avoid counting rotations twice?
investigations.deeper: Compare with 24 or 48 cubes. Predict which target gives more possibilities.
investigations.practical: 30 cubes and squared paper.

investigations.start: Inspect a 3 × 3 × 3 painted cube. Count corners first.
investigations.investigate: Record groups with 0, 1, 2 and 3 painted faces. Repeat for a 4 × 4 × 4 cube.
investigations.deeper: Predict one group for a 5 × 5 × 5 cube and justify it with a sketch.
investigations.practical: Sugar cubes or wooden cubes; paint or coloured paper.

investigations.start: Make two rectangles with perimeter 36.
investigations.investigate: Tabulate side lengths and areas. Which rectangle encloses the most space?
investigations.deeper: Does doubling each side double the area? Test and explain.
investigations.practical: String and squared paper.

investigations.start: Predict where a short sequence of moves will finish.
investigations.investigate: Use a repeat to trace a square. Change its size without changing its shape.
investigations.deeper: Explain how turning differs from moving up or down.
investigations.practical: Floor squares and arrow cards.

investigations.start: Rearrange a precut shape without gaps or overlaps.
investigations.investigate: How can you check that the area has stayed the same?
investigations.deeper: Compare two rearrangements: which lengths changed, and which quantities stayed fixed?
investigations.practical: Paper shapes, scissors and squared paper.

year5.gaps: Existing workshops retained; coverage and assessment require further development.

year6.label: Year 6

investigations.start: Mark squares and multiples on the same grid.
investigations.investigate: Which remainders can square numbers have when divided by 4? Gather evidence.
investigations.deeper: Explain your prediction using even and odd numbers.
investigations.practical: Counters arranged as square arrays.

investigations.start: Find every rectangular array for 48.
investigations.investigate: Organise your factor pairs so you know none are missing.
investigations.deeper: Compare the number of factors of 36 and 48. What is special about a square?
investigations.practical: 48 counters or squared paper.

investigations.start: Sort the small cubes in a painted 3 × 3 × 3 cube.
investigations.investigate: Build a table for side lengths 2, 3, 4 and 5. Describe each group in words.
investigations.deeper: Predict a larger cube without counting every small cube. Explain your method.
investigations.practical: Cubes and a table of results.

investigations.start: Rearrange a triangle or parallelogram into a familiar shape.
investigations.investigate: Use the rearrangement to explain an area rule. Identify base and perpendicular height.
investigations.deeper: Why is a sloping side not always the height?
investigations.practical: Two identical paper triangles and a ruler.

investigations.start: Choose one mother plant and no other plants or coins. Play one day at a time.
investigations.investigate: Record the coins earned each day and the running total. How are these different?
investigations.deeper: Describe a rule in words; use letters only when the pattern is secure.
investigations.practical: Counters for coins and beans for seeds.

investigations.start: Move a triangle with one side across the circle’s diameter.
investigations.investigate: Measure the angle opposite the diameter in several positions. What stays the same?
investigations.deeper: Can you explain it using triangles from the centre? This is beyond Year 6 core content.
investigations.practical: Paper circle, ruler and protractor.

year6.gaps: Further workshops are still needed for fractions, decimals and percentages, ratio, arithmetic, statistics and coordinate transformations.

year7.label: Year 7

investigations.start: Tile a rectangle by taking away the largest possible square each time.
investigations.investigate: Compare the last square’s side with the common factors of the original side lengths.
investigations.deeper: Explain why replacing a rectangle by the remaining rectangle preserves common factors.
investigations.practical: Squared paper and scissors.

investigations.start: Highlight multiples of 3 in grids of different widths.
investigations.investigate: How does changing the grid width change stripes and diagonals?
investigations.deeper: Describe the pattern using row number and column number.
investigations.practical: Printed number grids and coloured pencils.

investigations.start: Keep perimeter 36 and list several pairs of side lengths.
investigations.investigate: Call one side x. Write the other side and then the area in terms of x.
investigations.deeper: Explain why the areas rise and then fall.
investigations.practical: String and squared paper.

investigations.start: Build a shape and turn or flip it.
investigations.investigate: Decide when two shapes count as the same. Compare area and perimeter.
investigations.deeper: Design a systematic way to list shapes made from four squares.
investigations.practical: Four card squares per person.

investigations.start: Record daily coins and cumulative coins separately.
investigations.investigate: Find a rule for the daily increase, then predict the next total.
investigations.deeper: Explain why a constant increase in daily income gives a non-constant increase in total coins.
investigations.practical: Beans and counters.

investigations.start: Explain exactly what the feedback rules allow you to conclude.
investigations.investigate: Compare a guess intended to win with a guess intended to learn.
investigations.deeper: Count possible codes for a small version and eliminate them systematically.
investigations.practical: Coloured counters and candidate-code cards.

year7.gaps: Further workshops are still needed for signed-number arithmetic, fractions, decimals, percentages, equations and statistics.

year8.label: Year 8

investigations.start: Count edge cubes separately from corner cubes.
investigations.investigate: Describe the number of cubes with two painted faces for side length n.
investigations.deeper: Build and justify expressions for the other groups.
investigations.practical: A cube model and labelled sketches.

investigations.start: Connect numbered points on two straight edges.
investigations.investigate: Write coordinates for each end of a string. Change the pairing rule.
investigations.deeper: The visible curve is an envelope: each string remains straight. Describe this distinction.
investigations.practical: Card, ruler, thread and tape.

investigations.start: Rearrange a shape into a rectangle.
investigations.investigate: Compare an area calculation before and after rearranging.
investigations.deeper: Use the equal areas to justify an algebraic identity.
investigations.practical: Paper shapes and squared paper.

investigations.start: Predict what might vary when offspring are chosen at random.
investigations.investigate: Repeat the same settings several times and record outcomes at the same day.
investigations.deeper: Compare the mean and range. Explain why one run cannot establish a typical outcome.
investigations.practical: Coins, beans and a shared results table.

investigations.start: Track the same feature through two repetitions.
investigations.investigate: Describe the rotation and enlargement that take one copy to the next.
investigations.deeper: How do lengths and areas change under the same enlargement?
investigations.practical: Tracing paper and a ruler.

investigations.start: Use the square-removal process on two different rectangles.
investigations.investigate: Write the steps as repeated subtraction or division with remainders.
investigations.deeper: Explain why the process terminates for positive whole-number sides.
investigations.practical: Squared paper.

year8.gaps: Further workshops are still needed for ratio and proportion, equations, standard form, probability models and statistical displays.

year9.label: Year 9

investigations.start: Predict each painted-face group for side length n.
investigations.investigate: Expand the expressions and check that all four groups add to n cubed.
investigations.deeper: Explain the identity geometrically, including why small n needs care.
investigations.practical: Labelled cube sketches.

investigations.start: For perimeter 36, record area against one side length.
investigations.investigate: Plot the values and explain the symmetry about the best rectangle.
investigations.deeper: Write the area as 81 − (x − 9)². What does this show?
investigations.practical: Squared paper or a graphing tool alongside the activity.

investigations.start: Explore the angle subtended by a diameter.
investigations.investigate: Use radii and isosceles triangles to explain the angle relationship.
investigations.deeper: State assumptions and turn your explanation into a proof.
investigations.practical: Compass, ruler and protractor.

investigations.start: Predict which ramp path is fastest, then test.
investigations.investigate: Change one thing at a time. Explain why shortest distance need not mean shortest time.
investigations.deeper: Separate observations from a proof. The fastest-path mathematics goes beyond GCSE.
investigations.practical: A marble and flexible track, where available.

investigations.start: Collect results from repeated runs with identical settings.
investigations.investigate: Compare mean, median and range; graph the outcomes.
investigations.deeper: How many runs would make your estimate more convincing? Explain what remains uncertain.
investigations.practical: A spreadsheet or paper results table.

investigations.start: Build a small set of cards sharing exactly one symbol per pair.
investigations.investigate: Count symbol appearances and check every pair of cards.
investigations.deeper: Find a counting constraint before making a bigger set. Finite planes are an optional extension.
investigations.practical: Blank cards and stickers.

year9.gaps: Further workshops are still needed for simultaneous equations, inequalities, Pythagoras, trigonometry and probability trees.

gcse.label: GCSE

investigations.curriculumConnection: Foundation / Higher · HCF and problem solving
investigations.start: Find the largest square tile that covers a rectangle exactly.
investigations.investigate: Connect the geometric process to prime factors and HCF.
investigations.deeper: Explain why the same algorithm works for other whole-number dimensions.
investigations.practical: Squared paper and scissors.

investigations.start: Rearrange a shape to make its area easier to calculate.
investigations.investigate: Explain an area formula using the rearrangement.
investigations.deeper: Give a labelled argument that works for general dimensions.
investigations.practical: Paper, scissors and a ruler.

investigations.start: Write expressions for the four painted-face groups.
investigations.investigate: Expand and simplify; verify that their sum is n³ for n ≥ 2.
investigations.deeper: Explain the cancellation using the geometry, not just symbolic manipulation.
investigations.practical: A cube model and labelled diagrams.

investigations.start: Model the area of a rectangle with perimeter 36.
investigations.investigate: Use A = x(18 − x). Compare a table, graph and completed-square form.
investigations.deeper: State the domain and prove the maximum area.
investigations.practical: Squared paper and a graphing tool.

investigations.start: Make and test a conjecture about an angle in a semicircle.
investigations.investigate: Build a proof using the centre, radii and triangle angle sums.
investigations.deeper: Try to explain a second circle relationship without relying on measurement alone.
investigations.practical: Compass and straightedge.

investigations.curriculumConnection: Foundation / Higher · experimental probability · enrichment context
investigations.start: Repeat an experiment under fixed rules.
investigations.investigate: Estimate probabilities from frequencies and compare independent batches.
investigations.deeper: Discuss sample size, variation and the limits of an estimate.
investigations.practical: Spreadsheet or tally chart.

gcse.gaps: This is an investigation collection, not a revision course. Full number, algebra, ratio, geometry, probability and statistics coverage, exam practice and board mapping are still to build.

a-level.label: A-level

investigations.start: Write an area function for a fixed perimeter.
investigations.investigate: Differentiate to find a stationary point and justify that it is a maximum.
investigations.deeper: Compare calculus with completing the square; state the feasible domain.
investigations.practical: Paper for derivations; the activity supplies visual evidence.

investigations.start: Define daily income and total coins as separate sequences.
investigations.investigate: Derive a formula for the cumulative total from an arithmetic series. State your day convention.
investigations.deeper: Change the reproduction rule and investigate the new recurrence; more advanced recurrences are enrichment.
investigations.practical: Paper or a spreadsheet for symbolic and numerical checks.

investigations.start: Form expressions for the four painted-face groups.
investigations.investigate: Prove their sum equals n³ and interpret each term geometrically.
investigations.deeper: Seek another geometric decomposition that gives the same identity.
investigations.practical: Cube sketches and algebra on paper.

investigations.curriculumConnection: Statistics · simulation and expectation · enrichment context
investigations.start: Record the distribution of coin totals on a fixed day across many runs.
investigations.investigate: Estimate the mean and variance and compare batches. State assumptions about the random rule.
investigations.deeper: Derive expected growth using conditional expectation if ready; this extension goes beyond the standard course.
investigations.practical: Spreadsheet or code for repeated trials.

investigations.start: Compare ramp times and discuss the model’s assumptions.
investigations.investigate: For a particle released from rest without friction, use v² = 2gh to relate speed to vertical drop.
investigations.deeper: Explain why finding the fastest curve is a calculus-of-variations problem beyond A-level. Do not treat the simulation as a proof.
investigations.practical: Paper for a particle model; real rolling marbles also have rotational energy.

investigations.start: Describe a family of straight strings by equations.
investigations.investigate: Investigate the envelope by comparing neighbouring lines and their intersections.
investigations.deeper: Use a parameter to derive an envelope when ready; this is beyond core A-level requirements.
investigations.practical: Thread models, paper and a graphing tool.

a-level.gaps: This is an investigation collection, not a complete course. Functions, trigonometry, exponentials and logarithms, integration, vectors, distributions, hypothesis tests, forces and kinematics need dedicated teaching sequences.
